To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) our methods are capable of identifying and ranking the most relevant WSDs in a collection, and (ii) the ranking is improved by combining structural with semantic similarity.

(a) the structural matching method is able to identify the structural similarity of two web services, even when their structure is not identical, and (b) the semantic matching method is able, to some extent, to assess the semantic similarity of two services based on the similarity between their identifiers.

(i) a semantic information retrieval step can identify a small set of likely candidate WSDL specifications for the desired service; (ii) a semantic structure-matcher can further refine the list of candidates by assessing the structural similarity between the desired and the retrieved WSDL specifications; and (iii) a semantic identifier matcher can refine the list of likely candidates further by assessing the semantic similarity between the identifiers of the desired and the identified WSDL specifications.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of assessing the similarity between web-service specifications, and with the application of this similarity assessment to service discovery.
the problem of assessing the similarity between two web-service specifications based on the semantic and structural similarity of their elements and the semantic similarity between their identifiers.

the problem of assessing the similarity between two services based on the structure and semantics of their descriptions, and using these similarity assessments to identify the most relevant services to a given query.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the semantic matching approach is more robust than the structural matching approach, and the combination of the two approaches is more robust than either one alone.
the proposed methods are effective for service discovery and selection, and that their performance is highly dependent on the quality of the input data.
the methods we propose are able to identify a subset of the available services that is relevant to the user’s query.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a comprehensive and robust set of similarity assessment methods for web services.

we can achieve a precision of over 70% and recall of over 80% in the identification of relevant WSDL specifications, given only a textual description and partial specification of the desired behavior, and a precision of over of 90% and a recall of 80% when a full specification of the desired functionality is available.
the structural and semantic similarity methods are complementary and that they can be used in conjunction to improve the accuracy of web-service discovery.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, while structural matching is not very effective in assessing the similarity between web service descriptions, semantic matching of the descriptions' natural language identifiers can be quite effective in identifying relevant services.
a combination of structural and semantic similarity assessment methods can be used to effectively support programmatic service retrieval.

, while structural and semantic similarity assessment can be effective for the discovery of services that are very similar to the desired service, it is less useful for identifying services that are only somewhat related to the desired service.
